plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: Rows of goblet-shaped blooms stretch across the Dutch bulb fields in bands of crimson, butter yellow, blush pink and near-black purple. From a distance the fields look like a striped quilt laid over the flat landscape.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to early May, with the Dutch peak in mid to late April
plants.location: Bulb region of the Netherlands, including the fields near Lisse and Keukenhof Gardens
plants.funFact: In the 1630s tulip bulbs became so prized in the Dutch Republic that single bulbs sold for more than the price of a canal house. This episode is known as tulip mania.

plants.name: Wisteria floribunda
plants.description: Long, fragrant clusters of blossom hang from trellises and old twisting vines, forming glowing tunnels of lavender and violet. At night, special illuminations make the hanging blooms look like a waterfall of light.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-April to mid-May at Ashikaga, Japan
plants.location: Ashikaga Flower Park, Tochigi Prefecture, Japan
plants.funFact: Wisteria is a climbing legume. Its twining stems can grow strong enough to crush wooden structures, and Japanese wisteria twines clockwise.

plants.name: Cercis canadensis
plants.description: Before its heart-shaped leaves unfurl, bare branches and even the trunk erupt in clusters of tiny magenta-pink, pea-like flowers. The tree makes a bright haze of color along woodland edges and in suburban gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: April, for roughly two to three weeks in early spring
plants.location: Eastern and central United States, such as the Missouri woodlands and Midwestern gardens
plants.funFact: Redbud flowers are edible, with a mildly tangy taste. Some of them sprout straight from the old wood of the trunk and main branches, a trait called cauliflory.
